the study of higher dimensional operator corrections to Goldberger-Treiman relations.
the study of the goldstino interactions in supersymmetric extensions of the standard model.
the study of supersymmetry breaking.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the goldstino–MSSM interactions given by the GT relations are valid only below a certain energy scale, which depends on the mass scale of the messenger sector in the GMSB models.
the goldstino–MSSM vertices can be calculated from the superpotential and Kähler potential, and the Goldberger–Tremain relations are not valid above the mediator scale.
the goldstino–MSSM interactions are valid only below a certain scale, and above that scale they are not valid.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the goldstino–MSSM couplings are given by the Goldgerger–Treiman vertices at low energies, and at higher scales they are given by the supergravity vertices, with no mixing between the two.
the Goldberger-Treiman vertices are valid at energies below the scale of the messenger mass.
the goldstino–SUSY particle interactions are valid only below a scale of the order of the SUSY breaking scale.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the Goldberger-Treiman relations are not valid at the scale of the messenger sector and that the goldstino decouples from matter at this scale.
the goldstino couplings are modified by higher dimensional operators in a model dependent way, and the couplings can be used to distinguish between different GMSB models.
, at the messenger scale, the goldstino–MSSM vertices are not protected by any symmetry, and hence the goldstinos can decay to MSSM fields through higher dimensional operators.
